extracted.intended_audience: cognitive neuroscientists and psycholinguistics researchers studying humor/joke comprehension (MEG/ERP researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, analyzing, and interpreting MEG/ERP experiments that probe joke comprehension (funny vs congruous vs incongruous punch lines), including stimulus selection, time-window mapping to cognitive stages, and neural source interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis: within-subjects ANOVA and planned comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Values (ROI-averaged activity across time windows) entered into a within-subjects ANOVA and compared across the three levels of the Ending Type factor (funny, congruous, incongruous). The three-way comparisons were planned by virtue of the hypotheses and the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because comparisons were planned, reported p values were not corrected for multiple comparisons; nevertheless, the reported results need to be considered with prudence. Report pairwise contrasts and note when pairwise comparisons do not reach significance despite averaged differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexical–semantic stage (350–550 ms)
rubrics_metrics.description: A defined processing stage mapped to 350–550 ms post-stimulus (N400/N400m timeframe), associated with surface-level semantic analysis and initial associative relationships between setup and punch line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this time window to assess N400/N400m effects (semantic incongruity, priming). Expect anterior temporal and left inferior prefrontal generators; incongruous endings typically evoke largest activity here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity detection–global integration stage (700–1,150 ms)
rubrics_metrics.description: A later processing stage (700–1,150 ms) marked by protracted positivities (P600-like) reflecting detection of ambiguity/conflict and global coherence integration of punch line with context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this window to evaluate P600-like responses, conflict monitoring, and integrative processes. Expect contributions from anterior frontomedial, dorsolateral prefrontal, and left ventrolateral prefrontal regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: N400/N400m as index of semantic incongruity
rubrics_metrics.description: The N400 (scalp) and N400m (MEG) are sensitive to semantic incongruity; incongruous endings evoke the largest N400/N400m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret larger N400/N400m amplitudes as reflecting greater semantic mismatch; absence of difference between funny and congruous on scalp N400 may mask regionally specific MEG differences (e.g., LHAT attenuation to funny punch lines).

rubrics_metrics.name: P600/P600m as index of interpretive–integrative processing
rubrics_metrics.description: A large, protracted positivity (termed P600m) is greater to funny punch lines and may reflect interpretive–integrative processing, including conflict monitoring and combinatorial analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider P600m as indexing processes needed to resolve ambiguity and achieve global coherence; it can be influenced by task demands (plausibility/funniness judgments) and may overlap temporally with other late components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hemispheric and regional functional roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Different regions and hemispheres contribute distinct functions: LH anterior temporal/left ventrolateral prefrontal—predictive/semantic retrieval; RH—plausibility, divergent/weak associations; right dorsolateral prefrontal—sensitivity to funniness; anterior frontomedial—conflict/ambiguity detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting source estimates, map observed effects onto these functional attributions but note variability across studies (some find RH or LH dominance for nonliteral language). Use caution before asserting strict lateralization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface congruity / priming influences on N400 attenuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Surface-level semantic or phonological priming (synonym, repetition, category exemplar, phonological similarity) can attenuate the N400m, producing a 'surface congruity' that temporarily foils comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify associative closeness between stems and punch lines and report proportions (e.g., percent containing synonyms/repetition). Consider priming as an essential stimulus property that affects early stages, especially for puns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus categorization and composition (funny, congruous, incongruous)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stimuli should be classified into categories (funny, congruous, incongruous) and characterized by properties such as semantic/phonological association rates (e.g., percent with synonym or repetition, percent close semantic association).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report detailed stimulus lists and metrics (here: 28.8% of funny punch lines had synonym/repetition vs 8.8% in congruous). Such statistics are important to interpret N400/N400m differences and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke type specificity (puns vs semantic jokes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many stimuli in this study were puns; effects observed (e.g., left-lateralized N400m attenuation) may apply more to puns than to semantic (non-pun) jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state the joke categories used and be cautious about generalizing results across joke types; plan follow-ups to compare categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task design: rating for funniness vs passive comprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: Asking subjects to rate sentences for 'funniness' focuses them on humorous aspects and may bias observed late activity (larger P600 when making plausibility/funniness judgments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To dissociate understanding from decision-making, include response requirements orthogonal to predesigned funniness status and compare explicit judgment vs reading-for-comprehension paradigms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of stimulus probabilities to avoid oddball (P3b) confound
rubrics_metrics.description: Unequal proportions of funny vs not-funny trials (e.g., one-third funny) could introduce classical P3b oddball effects that overlap with late activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance rare and frequent stimuli (or control for oddball probability) and/or localize P3b generators to distinguish oddball-related sources from joke-related late prefrontal sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal variability and group averaging caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: The moment of 'getting' a joke varies across subjects and items, causing ramp-like, slow-rising late activity and temporal smearing when group-averaging, making it difficult to temporally dissociate ambiguity detection and global integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret late, slow-rising aMEG time courses with caution; consider paradigms or analyses that can better align or model per-item/per-subject integration latencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological choice: aMEG for temporal precision and regional estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Using anatomically constrained MEG (aMEG) provides temporal precision and regionally specific estimates of activity, offering insight into spatiotemporal stages of joke comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use aMEG to dissociate stages where possible, but be mindful of modality-specific issues (e.g., fMRI anterior temporal signal loss) and complement with intracranial EEG or fMRI as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of marginal and non-significant pairwise contrasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Group-level main effects may be driven by averaged differences even when pairwise comparisons with individual endings do not reach significance (some contrasts only marginally significant, p<.1 or p<.15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report exact p values, effect sizes, and allow for cautious interpretation of marginal effects; avoid overinterpreting non-significant pairwise contrasts even when omnibus tests are significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for future experimental controls and manipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Future studies should include balanced numbers of funny vs not-funny punch lines, response requirements orthogonal to funniness, better controlled setup vs punch-line matching, and parallel manipulations of explicit judgment vs comprehension to assess task effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments that isolate comprehension from evaluative decisions, control stimulus matching, and employ careful manipulations to probe dissociable stages of joke processing and potential gender effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual model: multistage joke comprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: Joke comprehension comprises (1) surface-level lexical–semantic analysis (N400/N400m) and (2) interpretive–integrative processing (ambiguity detection and global coherence integration) supported by a distributed frontotemporal network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this multistage framework to frame hypotheses and interpret temporal and regional effects; consider contributions from conflict monitoring and combinatorial semantic processes.
